To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high-spin states in (154,156)Yb nuclei have been investigated by the (144) Sm((16)O,4n)(156,154)Yb reactions, and the structural evolutions at large-angular-momenta have been discussed by means of the TRS calculations.
the high-spin structure of (156) Yb has been extended up to the 25(-), 31(+), and 33(-) levels.
high-spin structure of (156) Yb and structural evolutions at large-angular momenta in even-even Yb isotopes were studied by means of high-spin states in (16)O+144Sm fusion-evaporation reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure evolution of the yrast sequence at large angular momentum for the even-A Yb nuclei.
the structure evolutions at high angular momentum in even-A YB isotopes.
the structural evolutions in the yrast sequences of even-A Yb nuclei at large angular moment, and the results may provide a useful reference for the future experimental and theoretical studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, with increasing angular momentum, these even-A YB isotopes evolve from the vibrational structures to the rotational structures, and then to the superdeformed structures.
the even-A Yb nuclei undergo a gradual structural evolution from the soft rotor to the stiff rotor as the neutron number increases from N=90 to N=100.

the evolution of the structure in these even-A (156-164)Yb nuclei with increasing angular momentum is mainly induced by the alignment of a pair of nucleons from the Z=64 and/or N=82 core, and by a gradual increase in the deformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structural evolution of even-A Yb nuclei with increasing angular momentum is mainly induced by the alignment of neutron particles in the f(5/2) orbit, and the change in neutron number has an obvious effect on the alignment of the neutron particles in the h(11/2) orbit.

the evolution from quasiparticle-vibration to quasiparticle-rotation is the main reason for the structural evolution in these Yb isotopes with increasing angular momentum, and the neutron number plays a significant role in this evolution.

the structural evolution in even-A YB isotopes with increasing angular momentum is similar to that observed in even-A Gd isotopes, while the evolution induced by the increase of neutron number is different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural evolutions at large spin are sensitive to the proton and neutron numbers, and the proton-neutron interactions play a crucial role in the structural evolution of even-A Yb nuclei.
the structural evolutions in these even-A isotopes can be well explained by the TRS calculation.
the structural evolution in even-A YB isotopes with increasing angular momentum is similar to the evolution in the odd-A Yb isotones.
